Rashi on Ketubot 65a:10:1.english: He requested of the daughter of Rav Chisda - He requested marital relations from his wife.

Rashi on Ketubot 65a:10:2.english: With kulpei deshida - With the lock of a chest.

Rashi on Ketubot 65a:10:3.hebrew: קטלת לך תלת - שכבר ניסת לג' ומתו, כדאמר ביבמות בפ' הבא על יבמתו (יבמות דף סד:):
Rashi on Ketubot 65a:10:3.english: You have killed three - For she had already been married to three [men] and they died, as it says in Yevamot in the chapter [entitled] Haba Al Yevimto (Yevamot 64b).

Rashi on Ketubot 65a:10:4.english: To kill another - For you came to show your beauty so that a man would jump at you [to marry you].

Rashi on Ketubot 65a:12:1.hebrew: לחברך ולחברורך - שלא אתבזה על הבריות מכבודי הראשון, לא בפניך ולא בפני חביריך:
Rashi on Ketubot 65a:12:1.english: For your friends and for your friends' friends - So that I not be disgraced before people [by falling] from my former honor, neither before you nor before your friends.

Rashi on Ketubot 65a:13:1.hebrew: מפץ ומחצלת למה לה - הרי עור שטוח על מטה טוב מן המפץ. ומשני: באתרא דמלו פוריא בחבלי — במקום שאין רגילין לעשות שטיח עור למטה, אלא סירוגי חבלים:
Rashi on Ketubot 65a:13:1.english: Why does she [need] a soft mat and a hard mat - Surely leather spread over a bed is better than a soft mat! And [the Gemara] answers: "[In] a place where they fill the bed with ropes" — in a place where they are not accustomed to make a leather covering for a bed, but rather interwoven ropes.

Rashi on Ketubot 65a:13:2.hebrew: ומבגר לה - מצערי לה ומזקינין אותה, לשון בוגרת:
Rashi on Ketubot 65a:13:2.english: And [it] ages her - [They] cause her distress and age her; [the term is] an expression [related to] bogeret [a mature woman].

Rashi on Ketubot 65a:14:1.english: If it is her manner - The custom of the women of her family.

Rashi on Ketubot 65a:15:1.hebrew: אורחיה - דרכו לישן על כרים וכסתות, ואנן קיימא לן "עולה עמו":
Rashi on Ketubot 65a:15:1.english: His manner - His custom is to sleep on pillows and cushions, and we hold [that a wife] "ascends with him" [to his standard of living].

Rashi on Ketubot 65a:15:2.hebrew: כי אזילנא - ואני משרה אותך על ידי שליש, שקילנא להו בהדאי:
Rashi on Ketubot 65a:15:2.english: When I go away - and I am providing for you through a trustee, I will take them with me.

Rashi on Ketubot 65a:15:3.hebrew: וכי אתינא - ותשכבי עמי, מייתינא להו:
Rashi on Ketubot 65a:15:3.english: And when I come [back] - and you lie with me, I will bring them.

Rashi on Ketubot 65a:15:4.hebrew: ושקלת לדידי - מפץ שלי, או אם אקנה כר וכסת משלי:
Rashi on Ketubot 65a:15:4.english: And you will take mine - My mat, or if I buy a pillow and cushion of my own.

Rashi on Ketubot 65a:1:1.hebrew: אין ב"ד פוסקין יינות לאשה - שהיין מרגילה לתאות תשמיש:
Rashi on Ketubot 65a:1:1.english: The court does not allot wines to a wife - For wine accustoms her to the desire for marital relations.

Rashi on Ketubot 65a:4:1.hebrew: רגילה שאני - כיון דאינו חידוש לה, כבר דשה בו ואינו מזיח לבה:
Rashi on Ketubot 65a:4:1.english: [One who is] accustomed is different - Since it is not a novelty to her, she is already used to it and it does not stir her heart.

Rashi on Ketubot 65a:6:1.english: For pot-stew [tzikei kedeirah] - To flavor a cooked dish.

Rashi on Ketubot 65a:8:1.english: And they came to their house - And afterwards, “and Elkanah knew Hannah.”

Rashi on Ketubot 65a:9:2.english: Shufrazei - Tall goblets that they call maderins [fladerin] [in Old French].

Rashi on Ketubot 65a:9:3.english: Like this - [That is,] like the measure of my forearm and my upper arm.

Tosafot on Ketubot 65a:13:1.hebrew: ונותנין לה מטה ומפץ - אע"ג דלגבי סדור אמרינן בהמקבל (ב"מ דף קיג: ושם) דנותנין לו מטה ומטה ומפץ — משום דשמא גבי אשה לא הטריחוהו חכמים כ"כ, דאפשר לה שתלך ד' אמות אחר אכילה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 65a:13:1.english: And they give her a bed and a soft mat - Although regarding siddur [the assessment of a debtor's basic needs], we say in [the chapter] HaMekabel (Bava Metzia 113b and elsewhere) that they give him a bed, and a bed, and a soft mat — [here he gives her only one bed,] because perhaps regarding a wife, the Sages did not trouble him so much, since it is possible for her to walk four cubits after eating.

Tosafot on Ketubot 65a:13:2.hebrew: מפץ ומחצלת למה לה - ר"ת לא גרס מפץ ומחצלת, אלא ומחצלת למה; דמפץ הוא רך וראוי גם לסמיכה, ונהי דלשכיבה אין צריך — דהא אית לה מטה — לסמיכה מיהא צריכה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 65a:13:2.english: Why does she [need] a soft mat and a [hard] mat? - Rabbeinu Tam does not read [the text as] "a soft mat and a [hard] mat," but rather "and why [does she need] a [hard] mat?" For a soft mat is soft and is also suitable for leaning [on], and although for lying down it is not needed — since she has a bed — for leaning, at least, she needs [it].

Tosafot on Ketubot 65a:15:1.hebrew: ושקלת להו לדידי כו' - פירש בקונטרס: "ושקלת לדידי" — מפץ שלי. ואין להקשות: א"כ, תסגי לה בשני מפצין; דשמא מתוך שהוא מעונג, שעד עתה הורגל לשכב על כר, יטול שני מפצין לעצמו. ורבינו יצחק בן רבי מאיר ז"ל לא גריס "ושקלת לדידי", ואינה מתרעמת אלא שרוצה לעלות עמו ולשכב על כר, אע"פ שלעצמו אין לו עכשיו. וכן משמע, דלסתור טענה דקא טעין בעלה אליבא דרבנן קא אתי:
Tosafot on Ketubot 65a:15:1.english: And you will take mine, etc. - Rashi explained: ["And you will take mine" refers to] my mat. And one should not object: if so, let two mats suffice for her — for perhaps, since he is pampered, having been accustomed until now to lie on a pillow, he will take two mats for himself. And Rabbeinu Yitzchak ben Rabbi Meir, of blessed memory, does not have the reading "and you will take mine"; and she is not complaining [about her mat being taken], rather that she wants to ascend with him and lie on a pillow, even though he himself does not have [one] now. And so it is implied, for [Rabbi Natan] comes to refute the claim that her husband makes according to the Rabbis.

Tosafot on Ketubot 65a:2:1.hebrew: אחרי אכלה - כמו "אחרי אכלה" מפיק ה' משמע. ואף על פי שלא אכלה, כדכתיב: "ותבכה ולא תאכל", מ"מ אית לן למידרש הכי: "ותקם חנה" — אחרי שעת אכילתה שהיה לה לאכול, "ואחרי שתה" — אלקנה וביתו חוץ ממנה, שלא היה לה לשתות; ולכך "ויחשבה עלי לשכורה":
Tosafot on Ketubot 65a:2:1.english: After her eating [acharei ochlah] - It implies [a reading] like acharei ochlah [with a] mappiq he [i.e., "her eating"]. And even though she did not eat, as it is written: "And she wept and would not eat" [I Samuel 1:7], nevertheless we must expound [the verse] thus: "So Hannah rose up" — after the time of her eating, when it was [fitting] for her to eat; "and after he had drunk" — [referring to] Elkanah and his household, except for her, for it was not [fitting] for her to drink; and therefore [it states,] "and Eli thought her to be drunken" [ibid. 1:13].

Tosafot on Ketubot 65a:2:2.hebrew: שתה ולא שתת - מדלא קאמר "ואחרי שתותה" דומיא דאכילה שתלה בה, אי נמי "אחרי אכול ואחרי שתה", כדכתיב (משלי כ״ג:ז׳): "אכול ושתה יאמר לך"; ומדשני קרא בדבוריה, דריש הכי כדמפרש לקמן:
Tosafot on Ketubot 65a:2:2.english: "He had drunk," and not "she had drunk" - Since [the verse] did not say "and after her drinking" similar to "eating," which it attributed to her, or else "after eating and after drinking," as it is written (Proverbs 23:7): "Eat and drink, he says to you"; and since the verse changed its phrasing, [the Gemara] expounds thus, as it explains below:

Tosafot on Ketubot 65a:3:1.hebrew: אכלה ולא אכל - בתמיה, וכי תדרוש כמו כן שאין פוסקים מזונות לאיש:
Tosafot on Ketubot 65a:3:1.english: "She had eaten," and he did not - [This is asked] in astonishment: would you likewise expound that we do not allocate sustenance for a man?

Tosafot on Ketubot 65a:3:2.hebrew: מכדי בגוה קא עסיק קרא - דהא כתיב חנה בקרא, וכתיב נמי "אכלה"; אם כן, לכתוב נמי "שתותה", או לא לכתוב קרא בגוה ולכתוב "אכל ושתה":
Tosafot on Ketubot 65a:3:2.english: "Since the verse was dealing with her" - For Hannah is written in the verse, and "she had eaten" is also written; if so, it should also have written "she had drunk," or the verse should not have written [the passage] about her and should have written "he ate and he drank."

Tosafot on Ketubot 65a:4:1.hebrew: רגילה שאני דאמר ר' חיננא כו' - וא"ת: ומאי ראיה צריך על זה? דבברייתא גופה קתני "רגילה", משמע דווקא רגילה. ויש לומר: דר' אלעזר נמי איירי ברגילה, דאי בשאינה רגילה כלל בפני בעלה, פשיטא דאין פוסקין — דאטו יש לנו ליתן לה שאין בעלה נותן לה כשהיתה עמו? לכך צריך לאתויי מדרבי חיננא, שיש רגילה שנותנים לה, כגון שרגילה שני כוסות:
Tosafot on Ketubot 65a:4:1.english: "If she is accustomed [to wine], it is different, as R' Ḥinnana said," etc. - And if you ask: What proof is needed for this? For the baraita itself teaches "accustomed," [which] implies specifically [one who is] accustomed. And one can answer: [The statement] of Rabbi Elazar also deals with [a woman who is] accustomed [to wine], for if [it were dealing] with [a woman] who is not accustomed [to wine] at all in the presence of her husband, it is obvious that we do not allocate [wine to her] — for would we give her [that] which her husband does not give her when she was with him? Therefore, it is necessary to bring [a proof] from Rabbi Ḥinnana, that there is [a case of a woman who is] accustomed [to wine] to whom they give [wine], such as where she is accustomed to two cups.

Tosafot on Ketubot 65a:5:1.hebrew: אינה רגילה בפני בעלה אלא כוס אחד כו' - וזהו פירוש דברי שמואל: "רגילה נותנין לה כוס אחד" — היינו שרגילה בשני כוסות; ודקאמר "שאינה רגילה נותנין לה שני כוסות" — היינו שאינה רגילה שהיו נותנין לה שני כוסות, אלא כוס אחד; אין נותנין לה כלל שלא בפני בעלה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 65a:5:1.english: [If] she is not accustomed [to wine], in the presence of her husband [she is given] only one cup, etc. - And this is the explanation of Shmuel's words: "[If] she is accustomed, she is given one cup" — this means that she is accustomed to two cups [in the presence of her husband, and one cup when not in his presence]; and that which he said, "[If] she is not accustomed, she is given two cups" — this means that she is not accustomed [to the extent] that they would give her two cups, rather [she is given] one cup [in the presence of her husband]; she is not given [wine] at all when not in the presence of her husband.

Tosafot on Ketubot 65a:6:1.hebrew: לציקי קדרה - אברייתא קאי, כלומר: מברייתא לא תקשי, אבל מילתא דשמואל לא מיפרשא אלא כדשנינן:
Tosafot on Ketubot 65a:6:1.english: For meat pudding [tzikei kedeirah] - [This] refers to the baraita, meaning: there is no difficulty from the baraita, but Shmuel's statement is only explained as we answered [earlier].

Tosafot on Ketubot 65a:6:2.hebrew: לציקי קדרה - אברייתא קאי; כלומר, מברייתא לא תקשי, אבל מילתא דשמואל לא מיפרשא אלא כדשנינן:
Tosafot on Ketubot 65a:6:2.english: For pot-stew [tzikei kedeirah] - [This] refers to the baraita; that is to say, from the baraita there is no difficulty, but Shmuel's statement is only explained as we answered [earlier].
